claims.claim: On August 26, 2026, President Trump signed an executive order declaring a national emergency to ban or restrict high-risk foreign-produced equipment in the US electric grid.
claims.episode_span: On August 26, 2026, President Trump signed an executive order declaring a national emergency
claims.source_title: US Executive Order On Energy Grid Supply Chain Security
claims.supporting_quote: On August 26, 2026, President Trump signed an executive order declaring a national emergency to ban or restrict the acquisition and installation of high-risk foreign-produced equipment in the U.S. electric grid.

claims.claim: The order applies to generation, transmission or control facilities operating at 69 kilovolts or above and names large transformers, grid-tied inverters, circuit breakers, battery energy storage systems, SCADA software and industrial control systems.
claims.episode_span: operating at 69 kilovolts or above, including large transformers, grid-tied inverters
claims.source_title: US Executive Order On Energy Grid Supply Chain Security
claims.supporting_quote: The order affects equipment, hardware, software and firmware used in generation, transmission or control facilities operating at 69 kilovolts or above: large transformers, grid-tied inverters, circuit breakers, battery energy storage systems, SCADA software and industrial control systems among them.

claims.claim: Equipment used exclusively in local low-voltage distribution, including standard residential solar inverters and commercial distribution below 69 kilovolts, falls outside the order.
claims.episode_span: Equipment used only in local low-voltage distribution falls outside it
claims.source_title: US Executive Order On Energy Grid Supply Chain Security
claims.supporting_quote: Equipment used exclusively in local low-voltage distribution falls outside it, such as standard residential solar inverters and commercial distribution below 69 kV.

claims.claim: A covered foreign entity includes companies owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction of a foreign adversary, including Russia, Iran and North Korea, with China described as the real concern.
claims.episode_span: A covered foreign entity is any company owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction of a foreign adversary
claims.source_title: US Executive Order On Energy Grid Supply Chain Security
claims.supporting_quote: A Covered Foreign Entity is defined broadly: any company, national or subsidiary owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction of a foreign adversary.

claims.claim: Transactions after August 26, 2026 can be restricted, earlier equipment can be ordered removed, and US utilities are already pausing foreign-linked procurement.
claims.episode_span: Transactions after August 26, 2026 can be restricted, the Secretary of Energy can require earlier installs
claims.source_title: US Executive Order On Energy Grid Supply Chain Security
claims.supporting_quote: Transactions after August 26, 2026 can be restricted, and the Secretary of Energy can require equipment installed before that date to be monitored, disconnected, replaced or removed.

claims.claim: CoreWeave announced on September 30 that NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 is in limited availability, with Cognition the first production customer.
claims.episode_span: CoreWeave said on September 30 that NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 is in limited availability
claims.source_title: Cognition Is Running Impressive Devin Workloads on NVIDIA Vera Rubin
claims.supporting_quote: CoreWeave announced on September 30 that NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are in limited availability on CoreWeave Cloud.

claims.claim: Cognition measured up to 4.8 times higher total token throughput per GPU on Vera Rubin NVL72 versus a GB200 NVL72 baseline at matched interactivity.
claims.episode_span: Cognition measured up to 4.8 times higher total token throughput per GPU than a GB200 NVL72 baseline
claims.source_title: Cognition Is Running Impressive Devin Workloads on NVIDIA Vera Rubin
claims.supporting_quote: On SWE-2 inference workloads drawn from FrontierCode tasks, NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 4.8 times higher total token throughput per GPU than a GB200 NVL72 baseline at matched interactivity.

claims.claim: In CoreWeave testing, the Vera CPU produced more than 3 times faster agent-sandbox startup than an unnamed alternative x86 CPU.
claims.episode_span: the Vera CPU produced more than 3 times faster agent-sandbox startup than an unnamed alternative x86 CPU
claims.source_title: Cognition Is Running Impressive Devin Workloads on NVIDIA Vera Rubin
claims.supporting_quote: In CoreWeave testing, Vera produced more than 3× faster agent-sandbox startup than an unnamed alternative x86 CPU.

claims.claim: Microsoft first applied biomimicry at a Noord-Holland site in 2022, planting 150 native trees and more than 2,000 square meters of shrubs and grasses, and has expanded the practice to more than 20 sites.
claims.episode_span: planting 150 native trees and more than 2,000 square meters, about 21,500 square feet, of shrubs and grasses
claims.source_title: Can Data Center Design Choices Change Public Acceptance?
claims.supporting_quote: The company first employed the approach at a site in Noord-Holland, the Netherlands, in 2022, planting 150 native trees and more than 2,000 square meters (about 21,500 square feet) of shrubs and grasses around the campus.

claims.claim: UDN reports TSMC is planning a second US campus in Texas with six advanced fabs, Dallas the most likely location, and an investment that could exceed the $265 billion Arizona commitment.
claims.episode_span: six advanced fabs and Dallas the most likely location
claims.source_title: TSMC Reportedly Evaluating Texas Expansion Besides $265 Billion Arizona Plan
claims.supporting_quote: Citing semiconductor equipment industry sources, it says the project would include six advanced fabs, with Dallas the most likely location.

claims.claim: Reuters reported TSMC is evaluating a Texas investment, plans are not finalized, TSMC had not commented, suppliers have not been asked to prepare, and the board has not signed off.
claims.episode_span: plans are not finalized, and one source said it would come on top of the Arizona commitment
claims.source_title: TSMC Reportedly Evaluating Texas Expansion Besides $265 Billion Arizona Plan
claims.supporting_quote: Reuters has since reported, citing two people familiar with the matter, that TSMC is indeed evaluating a potential Texas investment, with plans not finalized.

claims.claim: UDN says Arizona still faces power and labor shortages while sorting water, after TSMC added another $100 billion to Arizona plans in July, and cites a tariff threat of up to 200 percent.
claims.episode_span: the Arizona site still faces power and labor shortages while it sorts out its water supply
claims.source_title: TSMC Reportedly Evaluating Texas Expansion Besides $265 Billion Arizona Plan
claims.supporting_quote: TSMC added another $100 billion to its Arizona plans in July, but UDN says that site still faces power and labor shortages while it sorts out its water supply.

claims.episode_span: fewer than 15,000 units in 2025 and possibly more than 6 million by 2035

claims.supporting_quote: Analyst reports from Goldman Sachs suggest annual humanoid robot shipments could reach more than 6 million units by 2035, up from fewer than 15,000 units in 2025.
